question.problem: Given that the intersection of the elliptic cone  ${x}^{2}+2(y-1)^{2}={z}^{2}$ and the plane $z=2$ is an ellipse, what is the length of its minor axis?
question.worked_solution:
To find the intersection of the elliptic cone and the plane $z=2,$ we substitute $z=2$ into the equation of the elliptic cone, and simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}+2(y-1)^{2} & ={z}^{2} \\ {x}^{2}+2(y-1)^{2} & ={2}^{2} \\ {x}^{2}+2(y-1)^{2} & =4 \\ \frac{{x}^{2}}{4}+\frac{(y-1)^{2}}{2} & =1 \\ \frac{{x}^{2}}{{2}^{2}}+\frac{(y-1)^{2}}{(\sqrt{2})^{2}} & =1\end{aligned}
$$

This gives us the equation of an ellipse with a semi-minor axis of length $b=\sqrt{2}.$ Therefore, the minor axis has length $2b=2\sqrt{2}.$
